literal: Gao Gan; younger brother Shen; younger brother Ang; younger brother Jishi; Feng Longzhi; son Zihui; nephews Xiaowan and Xiaoyan
idiomatic: Gao Gan; his younger brothers Shen, Ang, and Jishi; Feng Longzhi; Feng's son Zihui; and Feng's nephews Xiaowan and Xiaoyan

literal: Gao Gan, styled Qianyong, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.
idiomatic: Gao Gan, styled Qianyong, came from Tiao in Bohai.

literal: His father Yi, styled Citong, was a bold spirit with commanding presence, revered by his district.
idiomatic: His father Yi, styled Citong, was a man of heroic temper and striking bearing, held in awe by the whole region.

literal: At the end of Xiaochang, Ge Rong raised rebellion in Yan and Zhao; the court, because Yi was a leading magnate of Shandong, appointed him Administrator of Bohai at home.
idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, Ge Rong rose in rebellion across Yan and Zhao. Because Yi was a leading magnate of the east, the court appointed him Administrator of Bohai without requiring him to leave home.

literal: He had not long reached the commandery when the rebels grew stronger; Yi led the whole jurisdiction to relocate between the Yellow and Ji rivers.
idiomatic: He had scarcely taken office when the rebels swelled in strength. Yi gathered the entire commandery and moved it between the Yellow and Ji rivers.

literal: Wei thereupon established Eastern Ji Province, made Yi its governor, and additionally granted him General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Lecheng County.
idiomatic: Wei then established Eastern Ji Province, made Yi its governor, and further granted him the title General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Lecheng County.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Emperor Xiaozhuang, Yi held his territory and defended on his own.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Emperor Xiaozhuang, Yi held his borders and kept himself apart.

literal: He told his sons, "When the lord grieves, the minister is shamed; when the lord is shamed, the minister must die. Now the altars are in peril and gods and men alike burn with anger — to ruin one's house to repay the state, the time is now.
idiomatic: He told his sons, "When the ruler grieves, the minister is shamed; when the ruler is shamed, the minister must die. The altars stand on the brink, gods and men burn with anger — if ever a man is to break his house to save the realm, it is now.

literal: The Erzhu brothers are deeply suspicious by nature; where suspicion grows, harm follows. You should move against them early.
idiomatic: The Erzhu brothers are suspicious by nature, and suspicion breeds slaughter. You must strike before they do.

literal: Those who seize the initiative have the heart to take from others; the moment must not be lost.
idiomatic: The man who moves first already has the will to take what others hold — and the hour will not wait.

literal: " Before the plan could be settled he died.
idiomatic: " But the plan was still unfinished when he died.

literal: At the beginning of the restoration, posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the six provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Yin, and You, and Governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Wenxuan.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the restoration he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, grand guardian, recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Yin, and You, and governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.

literal: Gan by nature was bright and perceptive, tall and imposing, with knowledge and strategy; his voice and bearing were fine, and his movements altogether elegant.
idiomatic: Gan was bright and perceptive, tall and commanding, with a strategist's mind. His voice and face were handsome, his bearing altogether refined.

literal: In youth he was a reckless gallant and often broke the public law; when grown he reformed, lightly valued wealth and heavily valued righteousness, and formed many alliances.
idiomatic: In youth he was a reckless gallant who often ran afoul of the law; as a man he changed his ways, held wealth lightly and honor dearly, and bound himself to many allies.

literal: Yuan Cha of Wei, Director of the Palace Guard, held power in his age; he and Gan matched in spirit and treated Gan with great favor.
idiomatic: Yuan Cha, director of the palace guard, held the power of the age. He and Gan were kindred in spirit, and Cha treated Gan with exceptional favor.

literal: He first rose as Supernumerary Master of Writing for Attendant Cavalry, served as Attendant at the Rear, became chief clerk in the Grand Commandant's and Central Commandant's military offices, and was promoted to supernumerary master.
idiomatic: He first entered service as supernumerary master of writing for attendant cavalry, served as attendant at the rear, became chief clerk in the grand commandant's and central commandant's military offices, and was promoted to supernumerary master.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei still held a princely fief, Gan secretly attached himself to him.
idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei was still a prince, Gan secretly pledged himself to him.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Gan fled east to Yi.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Gan fled east to his father Yi.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, Gan was remotely appointed General of Flying Cavalry and General of the Palace Gate with Regular Attendance.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang took the throne, Gan was remotely appointed general of flying cavalry and general of the palace gate with regular attendance.

literal: The Gan brothers had originally harbored ambitions for independent power; seeing Rong slaughter men of standing, they judged the realm would fall into chaos, and so led the displaced people of Hebei in rebellion between the Yellow and Ji rivers, accepted office and rank from Ge Rong, and repeatedly defeated Qi Province's troops and horses.
idiomatic: The Gan brothers had long nursed ambitions of their own. When they saw Rong slaughter men of standing, they judged the realm would collapse into chaos. They led the displaced people of Hebei in rebellion between the Yellow and Ji rivers, accepted office and rank from Ge Rong, and repeatedly routed the forces of Qi Province.

literal: The court soon sent Right Vice Director Yuan Luo to pacify the three Qi regions; the Gan brothers led one another out to surrender.
idiomatic: The court soon sent Right Vice Director Yuan Luo to pacify the three Qi regions, and the Gan brothers surrendered together.

literal: The court made Gan Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: The court appointed Gan supervising secretary of the yellow gate.

literal: Erzhu Rong, because of Gan's earlier crimes, held that he should not again hold a post close to power; Emperor Xiaozhuang permitted Gan to resign and return home.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, citing Gan's earlier crimes, argued that he should not again hold a post near the throne. Xiaozhuang allowed Gan to resign and return home.

literal: Thereupon he gathered fierce warriors and took his pleasure in hunting with bow and hound.
idiomatic: Thereupon he gathered fierce warriors and passed his days hunting.

literal: When Rong died, Gan galloped to Luoyang; Emperor Xiaozhuang saw him and was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: When Rong died, Gan galloped to Luoyang. Xiaozhuang received him and was overjoyed.

literal: At that time Erzhu's partisans still held troops outside the capital; the emperor made Gan Grand Master of Golden Crown and Purple Radiance and envoy to Hebei, ordering him to gather his district as support within and without.
idiomatic: Erzhu's partisans still held armies outside the capital. The emperor made Gan grand master of golden crown and purple radiance and envoy to Hebei, ordering him to rally his homeland into a pillar at court and a blade in the field.

literal: Gan received the edict with tears; his younger brother Ang drew his sword and danced, asking to offer his life in service.
idiomatic: Gan received the edict with tears streaming down his face. His younger brother Ang drew his sword and danced, begging to die in the emperor's service.

literal: Before long Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; he soon sent his supervising officer Sun Baiyao with more than a hundred horsemen to Ji Province, claiming a general levy of civilian horses, intending to seize the Gan brothers when they delivered the horses.
idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and sent his supervising officer Sun Baiyao with more than a hundred horsemen to Ji Province, claiming a general levy of civilian horses — but intending to seize the Gan brothers when they came to deliver them.

literal: Gan had long nursed a mind for vengeance; when Baiyao arrived suddenly, knowing he was about to be trapped, he seized the initiative, secretly mustered strong men, seized the provincial capital by surprise, issued proclamations through the commanderies and prefectures, killed Baiyao, and arrested Governor Yuan Zhongzong.
idiomatic: Gan had long nursed a mind for vengeance. When Baiyao arrived without warning, he knew a trap was closing. He seized the initiative, secretly mustered strong men, took the provincial capital by surprise, sent proclamations through the commanderies and prefectures, killed Baiyao, and arrested Governor Yuan Zhongzong.

literal: He had Feng Longzhi provisionally administer the province, held mourning rites for Emperor Xiaozhuang, and the whole army wore white.
idiomatic: He had Feng Longzhi provisionally administer the province, held mourning rites for Emperor Xiaozhuang, and clothed the whole army in white.

literal: Gan ascended the altar to swear the host; his words were impassioned, tears and voice mingling, and officers and soldiers alike were moved to grief and rage.
idiomatic: Gan mounted the altar to swear the host. His words burned with passion, voice breaking through tears, and officers and soldiers alike wept with grief and fury.

literal: To the north he accepted the command of You Province Governor Liu Lingzhu and acted in concert with him.
idiomatic: To the north he accepted the command of Liu Lingzhu, governor of You Province, and acted in concert with him.

literal: Before long Lingzhu was killed.
idiomatic: Before long Lingzhu was killed.

literal: Just then the Grand Ancestor came out of Shandong, proclaiming that he came to punish the rebels, and the multitude was seized with fear.
idiomatic: Just then Gao Huan marched out of Shandong, proclaiming that he came to punish the rebels, and the whole host trembled with fear.

literal: Gan told his followers, "I have heard that Gao of Jin Province has heroic strategy that covers the age, and a will that will not rest beneath another man.
idiomatic: Gan told his followers, "I have heard that Gao of Jin Province has a heroic strategy that covers the age, and a will that will not rest beneath any man.

literal: Moreover the Erzhu are without the Way, murdering their lord and tormenting the people — this is exactly the moment for heroes to give their loyalty.
idiomatic: The Erzhu are without the Way — they murdered their lord and torment the people. This is the hour for a hero to prove his loyalty.

literal: His coming today must carry a deep design; I shall go with a light escort to meet him, secretly consult his intent — you need only put aside fear and let me go alone.
idiomatic: He does not come without a deep design. I shall ride out with a light escort to meet him and learn his intent in secret. Put aside your fear and let me go alone.

literal: " Gan then took a dozen horsemen to the pass to meet and pay respects.
idiomatic: " Gan then took a dozen horsemen to the pass to meet him.

literal: Gan understood the moment and was practiced in affairs of the age; his words were generous and matched the deepest intent — the Grand Ancestor greatly valued him and shared his tent and bed.
idiomatic: Gan read the moment clearly and knew the affairs of the age. His words were generous and struck the deepest chord. Gao Huan valued him greatly and shared his tent and bed.

literal: At that time though the Grand Ancestor inwardly held far-reaching designs, outwardly nothing showed; Erzhu Yusheng held Yin Province, and the Grand Ancestor secretly sent Li Yuanzhong to raise troops and press his city, ordering Gan to lead the host in feigned rescue.
idiomatic: Gao Huan already nursed far-reaching designs within, though nothing showed without. Erzhu Yusheng held Yin Province, and Gao Huan secretly sent Li Yuanzhong to raise troops and press his city, ordering Gan to lead the host in feigned rescue.

literal: Gan then entered with a light escort to see Yusheng and discussed military plans with him.
idiomatic: Gan rode in with a light escort to see Yusheng and discussed military plans with him.

literal: Yusheng went out together with Gan, and so was seized; Yin Province was thereupon pacified.
idiomatic: Yusheng went out with Gan and was seized on the spot. Yin Province was pacified.

literal: They also together settled the plan to establish the restoration sovereign; Gan was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Together they settled the plan to establish the restoration sovereign. Gan was appointed palace attendant and minister of works.

literal: Earlier, when Xindu was first founded and state and army were still in embryo, Gan had met with bereavement and could not complete his mourning.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Xindu was first founded and state and army were still in embryo, Gan had met with bereavement and could not complete his mourning rites.

literal: When Emperor Wu was enthroned and the realm was first settled, Gan memorialized asking to resign office and observe the three-year rites.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojuan was enthroned and the realm was first settled, Gan memorialized asking to resign and observe the three-year mourning rites.

literal: An edict permitted him to resign the palace attendantship while retaining the Ministry of Works, and enfeoffed him Duke of Changle Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: An edict permitted him to resign the palace attendantship while retaining the ministry of works, and enfeoffed him duke of Changle Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.

literal: Though Gan had sought withdrawal, he had not expected immediate consent.
idiomatic: Gan had sought withdrawal, but he had not expected consent so quickly.

literal: Once removed from inner attendance, he was rarely consulted on court affairs and was constantly discontent.
idiomatic: Once removed from inner attendance, he was rarely consulted on court affairs, and discontent settled on him.

literal: Emperor Wu wished to turn against the Grand Ancestor and hoped to use Gan; they met in the Huilin Garden, and when the feast ended the emperor kept Gan alone and told him, "The Minister of Works comes from generations of loyalty; today he has again achieved extraordinary merit. Though in name minister and lord, in truth we are as brothers — we should establish a covenant to deepen our bond.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojuan wished to turn against Gao Huan and hoped to use Gan. They met in the Huilin Garden, and when the feast ended the emperor kept Gan alone. "The Minister of Works comes from generations of loyalty," he said, "and today you have again achieved extraordinary merit. Though in name we are lord and minister, in truth we are as brothers. We should swear a covenant to bind our hearts together.

literal: " He pressed him earnestly.
idiomatic: " He pressed him earnestly.

literal: Gan replied, "Your servant has served the court for generations and received extraordinary favor; I have pledged my body to the state — how dare I be of two minds?
idiomatic: Gan replied, "Your servant has served the court for generations and received extraordinary favor. I have pledged my body to the state — how dare I be of two minds?

literal: " Though Gan gave this answer, it was not from his true heart.
idiomatic: " Though Gan gave this answer, it was not from his true heart.

literal: The matter arose in haste; he had not expected Emperor Wu to harbor a divergent design, and so did not firmly refuse, yet he did not inform the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: The matter arose in haste. He had not expected Xiaojuan to harbor a divergent design, and so did not firmly refuse — yet he did not inform Gao Huan.

literal: When Emperor Wu established personal troops, Gan privately told those close to him, "The lord does not draw near meritorious men, but gathers a pack of villains.
idiomatic: When Xiaojuan established personal troops, Gan privately told those close to him, "The emperor does not draw near meritorious men. He gathers a pack of villains instead.

literal: He repeatedly sends Yuan Shibi and Wang Sizheng back and forth to Guanxi to consult with Heba Yue.
idiomatic: He repeatedly sends Yuan Shibi and Wang Sizheng back and forth to Guanxi to consult with Heba Yue.

literal: He also sends Heba Sheng out as Governor of Jing Province, outwardly showing estrangement but in truth building a faction, placing the brothers near one another in hope of holding the west.
idiomatic: He also sends Heba Sheng out as governor of Jing Province — outwardly showing estrangement, in truth building a faction, placing the brothers near one another in hope of holding the west.

literal: Disaster is about to break out, and it will reach us.
idiomatic: Disaster is about to break out, and it will reach us.

literal: " He thereupon secretly informed the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: " He thereupon secretly informed Gao Huan.

literal: The Grand Ancestor summoned Gan to Bing Province and discussed affairs of the age face to face; Gan thereupon urged the Grand Ancestor to accept the abdication of Wei.
idiomatic: Gao Huan summoned Gan to Bing Province and discussed affairs of the age face to face. Gan thereupon urged Gao Huan to accept the abdication of Wei.

literal: The Grand Ancestor covered Gan's mouth with his sleeve and said, "Do not speak rashly.
idiomatic: Gao Huan covered Gan's mouth with his sleeve. "Do not speak rashly,

literal: Now I report that the Minister of Works is restored as Palace Attendant; all affairs of the Secretariat I entrust entirely to you.
idiomatic: Now I shall report that the Minister of Works is restored as palace attendant. All affairs of the secretariat I entrust entirely to you.

literal: " The Grand Ancestor repeatedly reported, but the edict in the end was not issued.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan reported repeatedly, but the edict in the end was never issued.

literal: Because his repeated requests were not granted, Gan knew turmoil was about to break out; he secretly informed the Grand Ancestor, asked for Xu Province, and was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander over the Three Xu Regions, Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: Because his repeated requests went unanswered, Gan knew turmoil was about to break out. He secretly informed Gao Huan, asked for Xu Province, and was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, area commander over the three Xu regions, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Xu Province.

literal: On the day he was to depart, the emperor learned that Gan had leaked the earlier affair and so told the Grand Ancestor, "I once privately swore a covenant with Qianyong; now he turns and wavers between two sides.
idiomatic: On the day he was to depart, the emperor learned that Gan had leaked the earlier affair and told Gao Huan, "I once privately swore a covenant with Qianyong. Now he turns and wavers between two sides.

literal: " The Grand Ancestor then took Gan's earlier memorials discussing affairs of the age, had an envoy seal and send them to Emperor Wu.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan then took Gan's earlier memorials discussing affairs of the age, had an envoy seal them, and sent them to Xiaojuan.

literal: The emperor summoned Qianyong to show them to him, confined him in the Secretariat, and had the Grand Ancestor's envoy reproach Gan for his earlier and later faults.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned Qianyong, showed him the memorials, and confined him in the secretariat, while Gao Huan's envoy reproached Gan for his earlier and later faults.

literal: Gan said, "Your servant has pledged his body to the state and exhausted loyalty to the end. Your Majesty already harbors a divergent design, yet you say your servant wavers.
idiomatic: Gan said, "Your servant pledged his body to the state and exhausted loyalty to the end. Your Majesty already harbors a divergent design, yet you say I waver.

literal: When a common man is falsely charged, escape may still be hard; how much less when the lord of men turns his hatred upon one — where then is escape?
idiomatic: When a common man is falsely charged, escape may still be hard. How much less when the lord of men turns his hatred upon one — where then is escape?

literal: If you wish to add guilt to a man, will words be lacking?
idiomatic: If you wish to add guilt to a man, will words be lacking?

literal: Great merit brings peril to the body — it has been so since antiquity.
idiomatic: Great merit brings peril to the body — it has been so since antiquity.

literal: If death brings awareness, I may yet be without shame before Emperor Xiaozhuang.
idiomatic: If death brings awareness, I may yet stand without shame before Emperor Xiaozhuang.

literal: " He was thereupon granted death, aged thirty-seven.
idiomatic: " He was thereupon granted death. He was thirty-seven.

literal: At the point of death Gan's expression did not change; all who saw it sighed in regret.
idiomatic: At the point of death Gan's expression did not change. All who saw it sighed in regret.

literal: At that time Military Guard General Yuan Zheng supervised the execution and asked Gan, "Do you have letters or words for your family?
idiomatic: Military Guard General Yuan Zheng supervised the execution and asked Gan, "Do you have letters or words for your family?

literal: " Gan said, "My brothers are scattered, each in a different place. In today's affair I think none will survive whole. My sons are still small and understand nothing; I fear nest overturned and eggs broken — what words are there to leave?
idiomatic: " Gan said, "My brothers are scattered, each in a different place. In today's affair I think none will survive whole. My sons are still small and understand nothing. I fear the nest overturned and the eggs broken — what words are there to leave?

literal: " Later, when the Grand Ancestor campaigned against Husi Chun and the rest and halted at Mengjin, he told Gan's younger brother Ang, "Had we early used the Minister of Works' plan, would we have needed today's campaign!
idiomatic: " Later, when Gao Huan campaigned against Husi Chun and the rest and halted at Mengjin, he told Gan's younger brother Ang, "Had we early used the Minister of Works' plan, would we have needed today's campaign!

literal: " At the beginning of Tianping, posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the ten provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, Qi, Xu, Qing, Guang, and Yan, Grand Preceptor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Wenzhao.
idiomatic: " At the beginning of Tianping he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, Qi, Xu, Qing, Guang, and Yan, grand preceptor, recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Wenzhao.

literal: The eldest son Jishu inherited his grandfather's marquisate of Lecheng County; the second son Luer was ordered to inherit Gan's rank.
idiomatic: The eldest son Jishu inherited his grandfather's marquisate of Lecheng County; the second son Luer was ordered to inherit Gan's rank.

literal: Gan's younger brother Shen, styled Zhongmi, was broadly versed in letters and history; his ambitions differed from his brothers', and his father favored him in particular.
idiomatic: Gan's younger brother Shen, styled Zhongmi, was broadly versed in letters and history. His ambitions differed from his brothers', and his father favored him in particular.

literal: At the beginning of the Wei restoration he was appointed Governor of Cang Province and Director of the Masters of Writing on the Southeastern Circuit.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wei restoration he was appointed governor of Cang Province and director of the masters of writing on the southeastern circuit.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to Governor of Guang Province, additionally made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to governor of Guang Province, additionally made grand general of agile cavalry and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: When the realm was first settled, Shen was permitted to bring several thousand men of his native district as personal followers.
idiomatic: When the realm was first settled, Shen was permitted to bring several thousand men of his native district as personal followers.

literal: Shen's governance was harsh and cruel, and he also indulged his attendants; officials and commoners suffered under him.
idiomatic: Shen governed with harsh cruelty and indulged his attendants. Officials and commoners suffered under him.

literal: When his elder brother Gan died, he secretly abandoned his province and intended to return to the Grand Ancestor; Emperor Wu ordered Qing Province to cut off his route home.
idiomatic: When his elder brother Gan died, he secretly abandoned his province and intended to return to Gao Huan. Emperor Xiaojuan ordered Qing Province to cut off his route home.

literal: Shen made his way by hidden paths to Jinyang; the Grand Ancestor made him Left Assistant Master of the Mobile Office, transferred him to the Masters of Writing, and in office he never shrank back — at the time all feared him.
idiomatic: Shen made his way by hidden paths to Jinyang. Gao Huan made him left assistant master of the mobile office, then transferred him to the masters of writing. In office he never shrank back, and at the time all feared him.

literal: After the banner of righteousness was raised, the people of An Province relied on their border fastness and would not submit to royal transformation; soon Shen was made Vice Master of the Mobile Office and led troops to suppress and pacify them.
idiomatic: After the banner of righteousness was raised, the people of An Province relied on their border fastness and would not submit to royal rule. Shen was soon made vice master of the mobile office and led troops to suppress and pacify them.

literal: At the end of Tianping he was appointed Palace Attendant and additionally made Opener of a Government Office.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianping he was appointed palace attendant and additionally made opener of a government office.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he went out as Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he went out as governor of Yan Province.

literal: Soon he was recalled as Director of the Imperial Censors; the censors he selected were mostly his kin and men of his district, not meeting the court's expectations, and Shizong memorialized ordering a new selection.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as director of the imperial censors. The censors he selected were mostly his kin and men of his district, falling short of the court's expectations, and Gao Cheng memorialized ordering a new selection.

literal: Shen's former wife was the younger sister of Cui Xuan, director in the Ministry of Personnel; Shen had cast her aside.
idiomatic: Shen's former wife was the younger sister of Cui Xuan, director in the ministry of personnel. Shen had cast her aside.

literal: Xuan was then entrusted by Shizong; Shen believed he was plotting against him. Shen's nature was narrow and hasty, and resentment accumulated in his heart; because of this he rarely impeached anyone and often let offenses pass.
idiomatic: Xuan was then entrusted by Gao Cheng. Shen believed he was plotting against him. Shen's nature was narrow and hasty, and resentment accumulated in his heart. Because of this he rarely impeached anyone and often let offenses pass.

literal: The Grand Ancestor reproached and blamed him; he grew only more ill at ease.
idiomatic: Gao Huan reproached and blamed him. He grew only more ill at ease.

literal: He went out as Governor of Northern Yu Province and thereupon held Wulao and surrendered to Western Wei.
idiomatic: He went out as governor of northern Yu Province, held Wulao, and surrendered to Western Wei.

literal: Shen entered the Pass first.
idiomatic: Shen entered the Pass first.

literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou led his host east; the Grand Ancestor defeated him at Mount Mang.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai led his host east. Gao Huan defeated him at Mount Mang.

literal: Shen's wife and children were about to cross west; on the road they were all captured.
idiomatic: Shen's wife and children were about to cross west. On the road they were all captured.

literal: Because his was a house of merit, the Grand Ancestor reported that only Shen's own household should be enslaved.
idiomatic: Because his was a house of merit, Gao Huan reported that only Shen's own household should be enslaved.

literal: Ang, styled Aocao, was Gan's third younger brother.
idiomatic: Ang, styled Aocao, was Gan's third younger brother.

literal: As a child he already had a warrior's spirit.
idiomatic: Even as a child he already had a warrior's spirit.

literal: When grown he was boldly unconstrained, with courage and strength beyond other men; dragon brows, leopard neck — his bearing was strikingly heroic.
idiomatic: When grown he was boldly unconstrained, with courage and strength beyond other men — dragon brows, leopard neck, a body built for war.
